reason: Implements the note tier's store over migration 0026's four tables: SqlNoteStore (nora/infra/sql/notes.py) and InMemoryNoteStore (nora/testing/note_store.py), bound by one shared contract suite (tests/contract/test_note_store_contract.py) both pass. Six verbs - create, standing, read, append_revision, search, record_miss. Four behaviours are load-bearing rather than incidental: create writes the note row and its first revision in ONE transaction, so head_revision_id never dangles and a note can never be a title in the injected index with no body behind it; append_revision is a compare-and-swap expressed as the UPDATE's own WHERE (spec 6.3), refusing a stale parent with a new StaleNoteHeadError rather than writing on top - the one edit made to nora/domain/notes.py; every read is scoped WHERE workspace = :workspace, so a note in another workspace answers None exactly as if it did not exist; and search joins note.head_revision_id = note_revision.id so it can only ever return head bodies, never a superseded one presented as current. search uses ilike with autoescape rather than the trigram similarity operator, measured against a real Postgres 18.4: the GIN index serves a parameterised ilike and narrows a 3+ character pattern, does not narrow a 2-character CJK one, and the planner picks a sequential scan at this tier's size anyway - so correctness rests on ilike's substring semantics, not on the index. record_miss upserts on (workspace, probe) in one statement, keeping first_seen_at and appending to observed_in only for a conversation not already there. Still no tools and no Dreamer adaptor above it - dormant, no code path reachable by users.
